name: eng-2176

cases.title: A format with parentheses matches its own titles

steps.why: wait for the discourse context under the title

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
cases.caption: The Draft Claim format is Claim, then draft in parentheses, then the content. A page in that format is now recognized as a Draft Claim, so it gets its discourse context.

expect.js: (() => { const uid = proof.uid('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation'); proof.assert(window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder.isDiscourseNode(uid), 'The page is not recognized as a discourse node.'); })()

cases.title: A title without the parentheses is not a Draft Claim

with.title: Claim draft - Naps replace a night of sleep

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
cases.caption: The parentheses are literal text now. A look-alike title without them is a plain page, where the old pattern treated them as a group and matched it.

expect.js: (async () => { await proof.sleep(800); const uid = proof.uid('Claim draft - Naps replace a night of sleep'); proof.assert(!window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder.isDiscourseNode(uid), 'The look-alike title matched the Draft Claim format.'); proof.assert(!document.querySelector('.discourse-graph-title-additions'), 'The look-alike page shows a discourse context.'); })()

cases.title: Node search lists the page under Draft Claim

steps.why: search for the Draft Claim page

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
cases.caption: Search finds it too: the node summoning menu lists the page under Draft Claim.

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.discourse-node-search-menu .h-64 > div')).some((section) => { const header = section.querySelector('.border-b'); return header && header.innerText.trim() === 'Draft Claim' && section.innerText.includes('Sleep improves memory consolidation'); }), { what: 'the page listed under Draft Claim' })

cases.title: The Draft Claim index lists the page and not the look-alike

steps.why: open its index, which runs the Draft Claim query

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
cases.checks: The Draft Claim index, which runs Roam's "is a Draft Claim" query, lists the Draft Claim page and leaves out the look-alike.
cases.caption: Roam's queries match the format too: the Draft Claim index lists the page with the parentheses and leaves out the look-alike.

expect.js: (async () => { await proof.waitFor(() => proof.dialogText().includes('Sleep improves memory consolidation'), { what: 'the Draft Claim page in the index', timeout: 15000 }); proof.assert(!proof.dialogText().includes('Naps replace a night of sleep'), 'The index lists the look-alike page.'); })()

cases.title: Sharing the Draft Claim page publishes only its content
cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.
cases.checks: The published concept's core_title is `Sleep improves memory consolidation`, not the whole title.
cases.caption: Roam extracts the content as well: sharing the Draft Claim page publishes Sleep improves memory consolidation, without the Claim (draft) prefix.

expect.js: (async () => { const uid = proof.uid("Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation"); proof.assert(uid, 'The page is missing.'); const row = await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 }); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === "Sleep improves memory consolidation", 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); })()

cases.title: A literal {v2} in a format no longer shifts which part is the content
cases.proves: Done When 2: One shared, unit-tested implementation of builder + extractor (at minimum: scan and builder share one grammar constant per app), and `DiscourseContextView` renders the same content string the converter publishes.
cases.checks: Sharing `Claim {v2} - Coffee helps focus` publishes the core_title `Coffee helps focus`. Roam's old scan counted {v2} as a placeholder that its builder never captured, and published the whole title.
cases.caption: Roam's placeholder scan and pattern builder now share one grammar: a literal v2 in braces no longer shifts the content, so sharing publishes Coffee helps focus.

steps.why: share the PK Versioned Claim page

expect.js: (async () => { const uid = proof.uid("Claim {v2} - Coffee helps focus"); proof.assert(uid, 'The page is missing.'); const row = (await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 })); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === "Coffee helps focus", 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); })()

cases.title: The default node types still recognize their pages
cases.proves: Done When 3: Formats without metacharacters behave identically to today.
cases.checks: The baseline Claim, Question, Evidence and Source pages are all still discourse nodes.
cases.caption: Formats without those characters work as before: the default Claim, Question, Evidence and Source pages are still recognized.

expect.js: (() => { const titles = ['[[CLM]] - PK baseline claim', '[[QUE]] - PK baseline question', '[[EVD]] - PK baseline evidence - [[@PK baseline source]]', '@PK baseline source']; const missed = titles.filter((title) => !window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid(title))); proof.assert(missed.length === 0, 'Not recognized: ' + missed.join(', ')); })()

cases.title: Sharing a default Claim still publishes only its content
cases.proves: Done When 3: Formats without metacharacters behave identically to today.
cases.checks: The baseline claim's published core_title is `PK baseline claim`.
cases.caption: Sharing a default Claim still publishes only its content.

expect.js: (async () => { const uid = proof.uid("[[CLM]] - PK baseline claim"); proof.assert(uid, 'The page is missing.'); const row = await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 }); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === "PK baseline claim", 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); })()

cases.title: Sharing an Evidence page with a source publishes only its content

steps.why: share the baseline source first, so the evidence's source resolves

cases.proves: Done When 3: Formats without metacharacters behave identically to today.
cases.checks: The baseline evidence's published core_title is `PK baseline evidence`: the content placeholder, not the source after it.
cases.caption: The default Evidence format has a second placeholder for its source, and sharing it still publishes just the content.

expect.js: (async () => { const uid = proof.uid("[[EVD]] - PK baseline evidence - [[@PK baseline source]]"); proof.assert(uid, 'The page is missing.'); const row = await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 }); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === "PK baseline evidence", 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); })()

cases.title: Format with star, pipe, caret, dollar, braces

expect.js: (() => { const qb = window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder; proof.assert(qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid("Q* | ^why do we sleep$")), 'The PK Pipe Question page is not recognized.'); proof.assert(!qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid("Q why do we sleep")), 'The look-alike matches the PK Pipe Question format.'); })()

cases.checks: The PK Pipe Question page is a discourse node; `Q why do we sleep`, which the old pattern matched through its | alternation, is not.

cases.title: Format containing a backslash

steps.why: open the PK Backslash Note type
open its index, which runs the type's query

expect.js: (async () => { await proof.waitFor(() => proof.dialogText().includes("Note\\ an idea worth keeping"), { what: 'the backslash page in the index', timeout: 15000 }); proof.assert(!proof.dialogText().includes("Note an idea worth keeping"), 'The index lists the look-alike without the backslash.'); proof.assert(window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid("Note\\ an idea worth keeping")), 'The backslash page is not recognized.'); })()

cases.checks: The PK Backslash Note index, which runs Roam's query, lists `Note\ an idea worth keeping` and leaves out `Note an idea worth keeping`.

cases.title: Create Relation dialog offers parenthesised nodes

do.js: (async () => { const caret = await proof.waitFor('.discourse-graph-title-additions .rm-caret', { what: 'the discourse context caret' }); if (!document.querySelector('.discourse-graph-title-additions button')) caret.click(); })()

steps.why: pick PK cites draft, whose targets are Draft Claims

expect.js: (async () => { const items = () => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-popover .bp3-menu-item')).map((el) => el.innerText); await proof.waitFor(() => items().some((text) => text.includes('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation')), { what: 'the Draft Claim page among the targets' }); proof.assert(!items().some((text) => text.includes('Naps replace a night of sleep')), 'The look-alike page is offered as a target.'); })()

cases.checks: With PK cites draft picked, the target list offers the Draft Claim page and not the look-alike without parentheses.

cases.title: Source placed before content resolves

with.title: PKS [[@PK baseline source]]: caffeine helps focus

steps.why: share the PK Source First page

expect.js: (async () => { const srcUid = proof.uid("@PK baseline source"); const uid = proof.uid("PKS [[@PK baseline source]]: caffeine helps focus"); const src = (await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=id&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(srcUid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 })); const row = (await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content,reference_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 })); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === 'caffeine helps focus', 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); proof.assert(row.reference_content && row.reference_content.sourceDocument === src.id, 'The sourceDocument reference is ' + JSON.stringify(row.reference_content) + ', not the source concept ' + src.id + '.'); })()

cases.checks: Sharing `PKS [[@PK baseline source]]: caffeine helps focus` publishes the core_title `caffeine helps focus` and a sourceDocument reference to the published baseline source.

cases.title: Regex characters inside the content survive sharing

steps.why: share the Draft Claim whose content has regex characters

expect.js: (async () => { const uid = proof.uid("Claim (draft) - a (b) [c] - d?"); proof.assert(uid, 'The page is missing.'); const row = (await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.120237&source_local_id=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(uid), { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the published concept', timeout: 15000, interval: 500 })); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === "a (b) [c] - d?", 'The published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); })()

cases.checks: Sharing `Claim (draft) - a (b) [c] - d?` publishes the core_title `a (b) [c] - d?`. The empty-content half is left to extractContentFromTitle's unit tests, since Roam trims a title's trailing space.

cases.title: Turning the Draft Claim specification on keeps the format's matching

do.js: (async () => { const box = await proof.waitFor('.roamjs-node-specification input[type=checkbox]', { what: 'the specification switch' }); if (box.checked !== true) document.querySelector('.roamjs-node-specification .bp3-control-indicator').click(); await proof.waitFor(() => document.querySelector('.roamjs-node-specification input[type=checkbox]').checked === true, { what: 'the specification to turn on' }); await proof.sleep(1000); })()

steps.why: turn the specification on, which stores a pattern built from the format

do.js: (() => { const qb = window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder; proof.assert(qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation')), 'The Draft Claim page is not recognized'); proof.assert(!qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid('Claim draft - Naps replace a night of sleep')), 'The look-alike matches') + ' with the specification on.'); })()

steps.why: check matching with the specification on

do.js: (async () => { const box = await proof.waitFor('.roamjs-node-specification input[type=checkbox]', { what: 'the specification switch' }); if (box.checked !== false) document.querySelector('.roamjs-node-specification .bp3-control-indicator').click(); await proof.waitFor(() => document.querySelector('.roamjs-node-specification input[type=checkbox]').checked === false, { what: 'the specification to turn off' }); await proof.sleep(1000); })()

steps.why: turn it off again, so the next run starts from the format

expect.js: (() => { const qb = window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder; proof.assert(qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation')), 'The Draft Claim page is not recognized'); proof.assert(!qb.isDiscourseNode(proof.uid('Claim draft - Naps replace a night of sleep')), 'The look-alike matches') + ' after the specification is off again.'); })()

cases.checks: With the Draft Claim specification on, which stores a pattern built from the format, the Draft Claim page is still a discourse node and the look-alike isn't; the case turns it off again and checks the same.

cases.title: Format with brackets and plus still matches
cases.intent: Make a node type with format `[[EVD]] + {content}?` (or reuse a default type with brackets). Create a page titled `[[EVD]] + a finding?`. Open the Node search dialog and the node type's index.

expect.text: The page is recognised as that type and listed in search and the index; a page `EVD + a finding?` without brackets is not.

decision.reason: default-formats-still-match covers bracket formats live, and the builder's unit tests pin that brackets, + and ? build the same pattern as before

cases.title: Format without {content} syncs the whole title
cases.intent: Make a type with format `Fixed Title (v1)` with no {content}. Create that page and share it, then look at it in Obsidian or the shared view.

expect.text: The node is recognised and shares with the full title as its content, with no error or blank content.

decision.reason: Roam already returned the whole title for a format without {content}; the changed side is Obsidian, covered by obsidian-format-without-content

title: Escape regex metacharacters in discourse node format expressions
claim: A node format with regex characters such as parentheses matches its own titles and yields its content in Roam and Obsidian through one shared builder and extractor, and ordinary formats behave as before.
given: test-3-graph has the four baseline pages; Draft Claim (`Claim (draft) - {content}`), PK Pipe Question, PK Backslash Note, PK Source First and PK Versioned Claim node types with a page and a look-alike each; a PK cites draft relation type from Evidence to Draft Claim; and Stored Relations on. The graph is signed in to the proof database and is in the eng-2329-demo group. The Obsidian cases live in the eng-2176-obsidian kit.

prepare.why: the extension has a proof database session for this graph; the proof database runs without edge functions, so this signs in the way create-space would
a Draft Claim node type whose format has parentheses, which are regex metacharacters
a PK Pipe Question type whose format has * | ^ and $

apply.js: proof.nodeType.ensure({ label: "PK Pipe Question", format: "Q* | ^{content}$", shortcut: "J" })

prepare.why: a PK Backslash Note type whose format has a literal backslash

apply.js: proof.nodeType.ensure({ label: "PK Backslash Note", format: "Note\\ {content}", shortcut: "K" })

prepare.why: a PK Source First type whose {Source} comes before {content}

apply.js: proof.nodeType.ensure({ label: "PK Source First", format: "PKS {Source}: {content}", shortcut: "X" })

prepare.why: a PK Versioned Claim type whose format has a non-placeholder {v2}

apply.js: proof.nodeType.ensure({ label: "PK Versioned Claim", format: "Claim {v2} - {content}", shortcut: "Z" })

prepare.why: a PK cites draft relation type from Evidence to Draft Claim, in the Global settings block, so the Add relation dialog filters targets by the Draft Claim format

check.js: (() => { const page = window.roamAlphaAPI.pull('[{:block/children [:block/uid :block/string :block/props]}]', [':node/title', 'roam/js/discourse-graph']); const global = ((page && page[':block/children']) || []).find((child) => child[':block/string'] === 'Global'); const rel = global && (proof.plain(global[':block/props'] || {}).Relations || {})['pk2176-cites-draft']; return Boolean(rel && rel.destination === proof.nodeType.uid('Draft Claim')); })()

apply.js: (async () => { const page = window.roamAlphaAPI.pull('[{:block/children [:block/uid :block/string :block/props]}]', [':node/title', 'roam/js/discourse-graph']); const global = ((page && page[':block/children']) || []).find((child) => child[':block/string'] === 'Global'); if (!global) throw new Error('No Global settings block.'); const draft = proof.nodeType.uid('Draft Claim'); if (!draft) throw new Error('The Draft Claim type is missing.'); const props = proof.plain(global[':block/props'] || {}); props.Relations = Object.assign({}, props.Relations, { 'pk2176-cites-draft': { label: 'PK cites draft', source: '_EVD-node', destination: draft, complement: 'PK cited by evidence', ifConditions: [] } }); await window.roamAlphaAPI.data.block.update({ block: { uid: global[':block/uid'], props } }); })()

prepare.why: a page in the Draft Claim format, a look-alike title without the parentheses, and a scratch page

apply.js: (async () => { await proof.page.ensure('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation', ['A Draft Claim page.']); await proof.page.ensure('Claim draft - Naps replace a night of sleep', ['Not a Draft Claim: no parentheses.']); await proof.page.recreate('PK format search scratch', ['']); })()

prepare.why: a page and a look-alike for each extra format, and a Draft Claim whose content has regex characters

apply.js: (async () => { for (const [title, text] of [["Q* | ^why do we sleep$", "A PK Pipe Question page."], ["Q why do we sleep", "Not a PK Pipe Question: no * | ^ $."], ["Note\\ an idea worth keeping", "A PK Backslash Note page."], ["Note an idea worth keeping", "Not a PK Backslash Note: no backslash."], ["PKS [[@PK baseline source]]: caffeine helps focus", "A PK Source First page."], ["Claim {v2} - Coffee helps focus", "A PK Versioned Claim page."], ["Claim (draft) - a (b) [c] - d?", "A Draft Claim whose content has regex characters."]]) { await proof.page.ensure(title, [text]); } })()

prepare.why: Stored Relations is on, so Add relation shows and a relation type without conditions counts

surface.area: Node type format in discourse node settings (Specification / format preview)
surface.why: DiscourseNodeSpecification now builds its format regex from the shared builder, so any format with regex characters is matched literally there.
CreateRelationDialog uses the shared inner-expression builder to decide which nodes fit a relation's target type.
Search filters pages by node type via the format expression; escaping changes which titles match.

surface.area: Discourse node queries (Datalog / query builder, node index)
surface.why: The re-pattern string sent to Roam's Datalog engine now contains escaped backslashes, which must survive the query encoding.

surface.area: Sync and sharing of nodes to the database
surface.why: Concept conversion, sync, and the cross-app converters take core_title from the new extractor, and the extractor now returns the title when the format has no {content}.
sourceIdOfNode was rewritten to use the shared matcher and a placeholder-order index, including a {Source} placed before {content}.

surface.area: Existing formats that relied on unescaped regex characters
surface.why: The old builder only escaped [ ] ? . +, so formats using characters like * | ^ $ { } or backslash were treated as regex; now they are literal.
